source_retrieval.scope: Only the downstream effect of the corrected endpoint-fibre formulation and the retained relative-consistency conclusion was checked; the unrelated proofs and ledger rows were not re-audited.
attempts: The two DOI resolver requests reached AMS but AMS returned HTTP 403 for the article and erratum pages.

Crossref's publisher-deposited record supplied the article abstract confirming relative consistency of ZF plus Countable Choice with failure of Urysohn's lemma; the erratum record confirmed the linked published correction but exposed no abstract.
Semantic Scholar independently exposed the same publisher-deposited article abstract and the erratum DOI metadata, but no erratum full text.
The AMS article page was recovered through a text mirror and supplied the same published abstract; the erratum full text remained unavailable there.

reviews.reason: The current remark uses cor-dmc-is-not-provable-in-zf only for the conditional ZF conclusion that DMC is not provable when ZF is consistent. The repaired supplier still obtains that conclusion from the published Countable-Choice model with failure of ordinary Urysohn separation and the unchanged implication DMC implies Urysohn. Replacing endpoint-image equality by the correct inclusions F subset f^{-1}({0}) and G subset f^{-1}({1}) does not alter either implication or countermodel; the remark itself states no endpoint-fibre formula and preserves the ZF/ZFA qualifications.

The repaired suppliers retain exactly the two clauses this status remark needs: DMC yields a separator with F subset f^{-1}({0}) and G subset f^{-1}({1}), while the corrected relative-consistency theorem supplies a Countable-Choice model in which that ordinary Urysohn assertion fails. Contraposition therefore still puts not-DMC in the same not-URY model. Such a model cannot refute URY implies DMC because its antecedent URY is false, so the endpoint-fibre correction does not change the remark's open-converse logic or require an item edit.

Within the repaired scope, the ledger says only that DMC implies Urysohn's lemma, that Countable Choice is relatively consistent with failure of Urysohn's lemma, and consequently that DMC is conditionally not provable in ZF. Those statements use the corrected separator condition by containment, not equality of endpoint fibres, and the published abstract confirms the retained relative-consistency conclusion. The item does not reproduce the defective equality formulation, and its conditional consistency wording remains explicit; its unrelated Baire, Stone, and Tychonoff rows were outside this downstream-impact review.
